newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel condemns Syrian bus bomb, denies connection.
newsitem.headline: Israel condemns Syrian bus bomb, denies connection.

text.p: Israel on Friday condemned a bus bombing in central Damascus that killed nine and wounded 44 and rejected Syrian accusations the Jewish state was behind the attack as an "outright lie".
"We unequivocally condemn terrorist actions in Syria and any place," the Israeli cabinet said in a statement released after its weekly meeting.

"The Prime Minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) said that the accusations published in Damascus accusing Israel of responsibility for terrorist attacks in Syria are an outright lie. We have no connection to the terrorist attack in Syria and Syria knows it," the statement said.
Syria said Israeli secret agents planted a bomb on a Damascus bus on New Year's Eve as part of attempts to destroy the Middle East peace process.
The Syrian accusation, which Israeli newspapers called "unprecedented", reflected the deterioration of relations between the two countries since Netanyahu was elected in May.

Netanyahu, who rejects the principle of trading occupied Arab lands for peace, has said Israel would not withdraw from the Golan Heights, the strategic plateau it seized from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Tensions rose in September when Syria redeployed 12,000 of its 35,000 troops in Lebanon to within striking distance of Israeli positions on the Golan.
The Syrian move caused war jitters in Israel but Damascus described the redeployment as a defensive move.

Israel's previous left-leaning government said it was willing to make at least a partial withdrawal from the Golan. Former Prime Minister Shimon Peres broke off talks with Syria last March after a spate of suicide bombings by Islamic militants in Israel.
Talks on the plateau's fate have yet to resume under Netanyahu.
